# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included to ensure secure HTTPS/TLS connections for git and other tools.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Install the compiled application into the specified install prefix.
RUN make install

# Copy the primary executable to a standard system path location (/usr/local/bin).
# This ensures 'kripke' is available in the PATH for direct execution without specifying its full path.
# The executable is renamed from 'kripke.exe' to 'kripke' for POSIX compliance.
RUN cp /opt/kripke-install/bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up source code and intermediate install directories to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke /opt/kripke-install

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included to ensure secure HTTPS/TLS connections for git and other tools.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# FIX: The --recurse-submodules flag is added to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Install the compiled application into the specified install prefix.
RUN make install

# Copy the primary executable to a standard system path location (/usr/local/bin).
# This ensures 'kripke' is available in the PATH for direct execution without specifying its full path.
# The executable is renamed from 'kripke.exe' to 'kripke' for POSIX compliance.
RUN cp /opt/kripke-install/bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up source code and intermediate install directories to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke /opt/kripke-install

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# FIX: Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The default Ubuntu 22.04 CMake (3.22.1) is too old.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Install the compiled application into the specified install prefix.
RUN make install

# Copy the primary executable to a standard system path location (/usr/local/bin).
# This ensures 'kripke' is available in the PATH for direct execution without specifying its full path.
# The executable is renamed from 'kripke.exe' to 'kripke' for POSIX compliance.
RUN cp /opt/kripke-install/bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up source code and intermediate install directories to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke /opt/kripke-install

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: The 'make install' step does not reliably place the executable in the install prefix.
# Instead, copy the executable directly from the build directory to a system PATH location.
# This ensures 'kripke' is available for direct execution.
# The executable is renamed from 'kripke.exe' to 'kripke' for POSIX compliance.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The intermediate install directory is no longer needed with the direct copy approach.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Correct the executable name for the cp command. On Linux, the compiled
# binary is 'kripke', not 'kripke.exe'. This ensures the executable is correctly
# copied to a system PATH location.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The intermediate install directory is no longer needed with the direct copy approach.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Defines a clean location for the installed binaries and libraries.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/kripke-install \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Add 'make install' to place the compiled binaries into the CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX directory.
# This provides a clean and predictable location for the final executable.
RUN make install

# FIX: Update the 'cp' command to use the correct path from the install directory.
# The executable is copied from the install prefix to a system PATH location for direct access.
RUN cp /opt/kripke-install/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code and installation directories to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke /opt/kripke-install

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
# FIX: CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX is removed as the 'make install' step is unreliable and has been bypassed.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Bypass the unreliable 'make install' step. Copy the compiled Kripke executable
# directly from its location in the build directory to a system PATH for direct access.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Correct the path to the compiled Kripke executable. By default, it is
# located in the build directory root, not in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Correct the path to the compiled Kripke executable. The build system
# places the binary directly in the build directory, not in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# Add the Kitware APT repository to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is used to ensure dependencies like BLT are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Correct the path to the compiled Kripke executable. The build system
# places the binary directly in the build directory, not in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included for secure HTTPS/TLS connections.
# The Kitware APT repository is added to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies,
# as the default version in Ubuntu 22.04 (3.22.1) is insufficient.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included for secure HTTPS/TLS connections.
# The Kitware APT repository is added to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies,
# as the default version in Ubuntu 22.04 (3.22.1) is insufficient.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

    wget && \

    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access. The build system
# places the binary in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included for secure HTTPS/TLS connections.
# The Kitware APT repository is added to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies,
# as the default version in Ubuntu 22.04 (3.22.1) is insufficient.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access. The build system
# places the binary in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included for secure HTTPS/TLS connections.
# The Kitware APT repository is added to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies,
# as the default version in Ubuntu 22.04 (3.22.1) is insufficient.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access. The build system
# places the binary in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access. The build system
# places the binary in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# This provides a modern, stable base with a rich package ecosystem.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This Dockerfile builds the Kripke HPC application with MPI support.
# It is designed for CPU-based Kubernetes environments, such as AWS EC2 instances.
# Per instructions, this is a single-stage build, and all build tools will remain in the final image.

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git for source control, and OpenMPI for parallel execution.
# The 'ca-certificates' package is included for secure HTTPS/TLS connections.
# The Kitware APT repository is added to install a version of CMake (>= 3.23) required by Kripke's dependencies,
# as the default version in Ubuntu 22.04 (3.22.1) is insufficient.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list > /dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for optimal performance and compatibility in containerized environments.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT: Required as we are operating as the root user.
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Disables a shared memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows MPI processes to be mapped to oversubscribed cores, common in Kubernetes.
# OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib: Disables the InfiniBand transport layer by default, ensuring fallback to TCP on standard cloud networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Set a working directory for downloading and building the source code.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke source code from the 'main' branch of the official repository.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to ensure dependencies like the BLT build system are cloned as well.
# No COPY or ADD instructions are used, as per constraints.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Create a build directory and enter it to keep the source tree clean.
WORKDIR /opt/Kripke/build

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Compiles with optimizations for production performance.
RUN cmake -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          ..

# Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable directly from its location in the build directory
# to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin) for direct access. The build system
# places the binary in a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/Kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Reset the working directory to the root for a clean final state.
WORKDIR /

# An entrypoint or command is not defined, as it will be specified by the Kubernetes job/pod spec.
# To run kripke, the user can invoke `mpirun` in their pod command, for example:
# mpirun -np 4 kripke --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8
